kurz: A pan is hot enough when a drop of water dances across it as a little ball instead of evaporating with a hiss.
bild_im_kopf: Like an air hockey puck: above a certain heat, the drop floats on its own cushion of steam.
was_passiert: At medium heat a drop evaporates at once with a hiss. If the pan is much hotter, a layer of steam forms under the drop and it glides on it. With stainless steel this is also the moment from which meat and fish stick less.
warum_wichtig: The most common cause of grey meat and sticking fish is a pan that is too cold.
schritte: Heat the empty pan over medium-high heat for 3–5 minutes.
Flick in a few drops of water.
If they dance as little balls, it is ready. Wipe away the water, add oil and wait briefly.
Do not overheat non-stick pans while empty; preheat those only with oil.
